intro: BBC Sport has put together a full compilation of the 13 Premier League goals scored by Danny Welbeck last season, highlighting every finish from a campaign that included three strikes against his new club, Chelsea. The video package gives fans a chance to review the form that preceded Welbeck's move to Stamford Bridge and to see how he delivered in different moments throughout the top-flight season.

sections.heading: A full-season highlights reel: what the compilation shows
sections.text:
The BBC Sport clip assembles all 13 of Welbeck's Premier League goals from last season in one sequence, offering a convenient way to assess the striker's finishing and movement across multiple fixtures. Viewers can watch the variety in his goal-scoring — from composed finishes inside the area to opportunistic strikes — and get a sense of his attacking instincts over the course of a single campaign.

Importantly, the compilation underlines a personal detail that will interest Chelsea supporters: three of those 13 goals were scored against Chelsea. That fact is presented as part of the season review and invites closer scrutiny of how Welbeck performed specifically when facing his new employers.

sections.heading: Why this matters for Chelsea supporters and wider Premier League followers
sections.text:
For Chelsea fans the footage provides a preview of the kinds of contributions their new signing delivered most recently. Watching a player's previous goals can help followers understand his tendencies in build-up play, his positional sense in attacking transitions, and the types of situations from which he tends to score.

From a broader Premier League perspective, goal compilations such as the one produced by BBC Sport are useful reference points. They allow analysts and viewers to revisit a forward's defining moments across a season and to compare those outputs with other attacking options in the division. While a highlights reel does not tell the whole story — it selects scoring moments rather than showing defensive work, link-up play or off-the-ball movement — it is a focused resource for judging finishing ability and composure in front of goal.

analysis: Seeing a player’s full set of goals from one campaign can inform opinions about form and suitability, but it should be treated as one piece of the puzzle. Analysts might view Welbeck’s compilation as evidence of a forward who can find the net in a variety of ways, yet managers and scouts will also consider work-rate, tactical fit, injury history and training performance when judging overall value to a squad. For Chelsea, the video may suggest potential tactical options — for example, using Welbeck in roles where his finishing and movement can be maximised — but such interpretations remain speculative without insight from the club and coaching staff.
